pinterest.title: Greece Wedding Packages: What a Greek Venue Package Usually Includes
pinterest.description: Elounda Beach on Crete publishes an indicative wedding package built around a dedicated consultant and a civil or religious ceremony, with a bouquet and boutonniere, sparkling wine and Greek wedding sweets after the ceremony, a wedding cake and a massage for the couple the day before. Flowers for the wedding location, photography and video sit outside it as additional services. See what Greek packages cover, venue by venue, and what to ask in writing.

pinterest.title: Civil, Greek Orthodox or Symbolic: Choosing Greece Wedding Packages by Ceremony
pinterest.description: The first question for any Greek package is which ceremony it is built for. The Elounda Collection, which takes in Elounda Peninsula, Porto Elounda and Elounda Mare, publishes separate civil, Orthodox and symbolic packages, each with its own documents. Symbolic weddings and vow renewals are not legally recognised in Greece. For a legal wedding, documents are Apostille-certified, translated into Greek and issued within three months of the date.

pinterest.title: What Greece Wedding Packages Leave Out: Exclusive Use, Rooms and Transfers
pinterest.description: The gaps in a Greek package sit in the conditions. Grace Hotel in Santorini prices weddings as a venue fee, not a package, and requires a wedding planner for every wedding. The Elounda Collection asks for a minimum three-night stay, and Abaton's terms set a minimum of 10 rooms for two nights. None of the packages in our guide publishes airport transfers for guests. Take our ten-point checklist into every quote before you pay a deposit.

instagram_carousel.caption:
What does a Greek wedding package actually include?

Most Greek venue packages cover the ceremony, its set-up, a coordinator and some help with the paperwork. Guest rooms, exclusive use of a space, transfers and outside suppliers are where they part ways, and each venue draws that line in its own place.

Our new guide sets out what each kind of package covers, venue by venue, across Crete, Santorini, Mykonos, Rhodes, Corfu and the Athens Riviera. It covers named tiers at Nana Princess, separate civil, Orthodox and symbolic packages at the Elounda Collection, and Grace Hotel's venue fee approach in Santorini.

The short version: check which ceremony a package is built for, ask whether the space is yours alone, read the room and night conditions, and find out who pays the town hall or church fees. Then put two quotes on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights and currency before you pay any deposit. If one quote answers a point and the other is silent, the silent one is not cheaper. It is unfinished.

Comparing Greek packages for your own wedding? Send us a message with your date, guest count and the venues you have in mind, and a Wedded Advisor will help you read them side by side. Your advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit. Full guide at the link in our bio.
